group: Unit i — RRTS / High Speed Operations
title: Normal, Degraded & Abnormal Modes + Operations–Maintenance Coordination

questions.q: Normal mode of operation means:
options: One system has failed and trains run slower
All systems healthy, automatic working, full timetable with Automatic Train Operation (ATO)
An accident has occurred and service is stopped
questions.explain: Normal = everything works, priority is punctuality plus comfort.

questions.q: In normal mode, the authority for train movement comes from:
options: The timetable and the signalling system
questions.explain: Normal working runs on timetable + signalling, automatically.

questions.q: Degraded mode of operation means:
options: A partial failure — one system, track or train affected — with trains still running at reduced speed/capacity using fallback procedures
Life is at risk and all service stops
The line is closed for the whole day
questions.explain: Degraded = something failed, but service continues safely at a lower level — like a car on a stepney.

questions.q: Abnormal / emergency mode applies when:
options: Automatic Train Operation (ATO) fails on one train
There is an accident, fire, major failure or external event threatening life
questions.explain: Automatic Train Operation (ATO) failure alone is degraded; danger to life makes it abnormal.

questions.q: In degraded mode, the priority is:
options: Safety first, then maximum possible service
questions.explain: Punctuality is sacrificed in degraded mode; safety never is.

questions.q: In abnormal/emergency mode, the only priority is:
questions.explain: In abnormal mode, rescue and evacuation take over; service stops being the priority.

questions.q: In degraded mode, train service in the affected area is:
options: Always stopped for the full day
Run at higher speed to compensate
Continued at reduced speed/capacity, possibly with single-line working or bus bridging
questions.explain: Degraded working keeps a reduced service moving under manual/restricted modes.

questions.q: In abnormal mode, train service in the affected area is:
options: Stopped or suspended while rescue and evacuation take over
questions.explain: Abnormal = service stopped/suspended in the affected area; life safety only.

questions.q: Single-line working — one track used for trains in both directions — is an example of:
questions.explain: One track both ways means reduced capacity — a classic degraded-mode method.

questions.q: After an Automatic Train Operation (ATO) failure, a train runs manually under Automatic Train Protection (ATP) protection. This is:
questions.explain: Manual driving under Automatic Train Protection (ATP) after Automatic Train Operation (ATO) failure is a listed degraded-mode example.

questions.q: A train develops a fault and runs at a restricted speed to the next station. The mode is:
questions.explain: Partial failure with reduced speed = degraded; service continues with human help replacing the failed machine.

questions.q: A fire is reported on a train at a station. The working mode becomes:
options: Degraded — trains keep running slowly past it
Abnormal / emergency — life safety takes over and service in the area stops
questions.explain: Fire is an abnormal event: stop, protect life, evacuate — service is no longer the priority.

questions.q: A car journey analogy: driving on a stepney at 40 kmph after a puncture is like:
questions.explain: Stepney driving = reduced speed with a fallback — exactly degraded mode. An accident needing an ambulance is abnormal.

questions.q: Authority in degraded mode rests on:
options: Operations Control Centre (OCC) instructions plus the degraded-mode rules
questions.explain: Degraded working is authorised and directed by Operations Control Centre (OCC) under special rules.

questions.q: Authority in abnormal/emergency mode rests on:
options: Incident command — Operations Control Centre (OCC) / the emergency plan
questions.explain: Emergencies run under incident command as per the emergency plan.

questions.q: Why does 'naming the mode correctly' matter in the exam and on duty?
options: Because the mode decides the speed, the authority and the communication level to be used
Because it is only a formality
questions.explain: Normal, degraded and abnormal each have different speeds, authorities and communication — a favourite exam point.

questions.q: A passenger is found on the track. This situation is treated as:
options: Abnormal — threat to life; protect the section and stop movements as directed
questions.explain: A person on the track is a life-safety event: abnormal mode, movements protected/stopped.

questions.q: Bus bridging is used in degraded/abnormal working to:
options: Carry passengers by bus past an affected section where trains cannot run normally
questions.explain: Bus bridging keeps passengers moving when rail capacity is lost on a section.

questions.q: Operations and Maintenance departments conflict naturally because:
options: Operations needs maximum service hours; Maintenance needs track access to repair and inspect
Operations wants to cancel all trains
questions.explain: Coordination is the daily negotiation so both get their time safely.

questions.q: Maintenance access to the track is normally planned:
options: As possessions, usually in non-revenue / night hours
By stopping any train on request
questions.explain: Planned possessions in the night window are the backbone of Ops-Maintenance coordination.

questions.q: Ops-Maintenance coordination is done through:
options: Joint planning — work permits, possession calendars, and hand-over/hand-back certification
questions.explain: Permits, calendars and certified hand-back make the sharing of track safe.

questions.q: A work permit system ensures that:
options: No work starts without protection for the workers and the track
questions.explain: No work starts without protection — a core coordination rule.

questions.q: Before train service resumes after maintenance work, what is essential?
options: Fitness certification at hand-back — no service resumes without it
questions.explain: Hand-back with fitness certification is compulsory before the line returns to service.

questions.q: Scenario: Maintenance asks for track access at 6 p.m. in the peak to fix a minor, non-urgent defect. The correct approach is:
options: Refuse peak access for non-urgent work; plan it in the night possession window
Let the fitter work between trains
questions.explain: Non-urgent work waits for the planned night possession; peak service and safety both matter.

questions.q: Scenario: A maintenance team finishes work but has not given hand-back fitness certification. Trains should:
options: Resume slowly on the Station Controller's guess
Not resume until the certified hand-back is received
Resume only empty trains at full speed
Resume because the shift is ending
questions.explain: No fitness certificate = no service resumption, whatever the time pressure.

questions.q: Scenario: Signalling fails on one section at 8 a.m. Trains can still run there at reduced speed under Operations Control Centre (OCC)-directed restricted working. This is:
options: The end of service for the day
Degraded mode — safety first, then maximum possible service
questions.explain: Partial failure + reduced working under Operations Control Centre (OCC) = degraded mode.

questions.q: Scenario: A derailment with injuries is reported. The FIRST priority for everyone is:
options: Life safety — rescue, medical help and protecting the site, under incident command
questions.explain: Derailment with injuries is abnormal mode: life safety only.

questions.q: The night maintenance window exists because:
options: After the last train, the track can be possessed safely for maintenance without affecting service
Passengers do not travel at night at all
questions.explain: Roll-in of the last train opens the window; roll-out ends it — the daily Ops-Maintenance timetable.

questions.q: Hand-over of a section to Maintenance means:
options: Trains keep running through the work site
Operations formally gives the protected section to Maintenance for work, under a permit/possession
questions.explain: Hand-over is formal and protected; hand-back returns it with fitness certification.

questions.q: During degraded working, communication between Operations Control Centre (OCC), stations and trains should be:
options: Clear, disciplined and as per the degraded-mode instructions — every instruction logged
questions.explain: Degraded mode raises the communication level; Operations Control Centre (OCC) instructions are logged and recorded.

questions.q: Which combination correctly matches mode with priority?
options: Normal — life safety only; Abnormal — punctuality
Degraded — revenue first; Normal — safety last
Normal — punctuality + comfort; Degraded — safety + maximum service; Abnormal — life safety only
questions.explain: This priority ladder is the master comparison of Unit i — learn it by heart.

questions.q: A track defect is found and a Temporary Speed Restriction is imposed while trains keep running. The line is in:
questions.explain: Trains running slower due to a defect = reduced capacity working = degraded.

questions.q: Two departments plan the week's engineering work together in advance. This is an example of:
options: Ops-Maintenance coordination through the possession calendar
questions.explain: Advance joint planning of possessions is coordination in action.

questions.q: In degraded mode, who decides whether to run single-line working or arrange bus bridging?
options: Operations Control Centre (OCC), as part of regulation and incident management
questions.explain: Operations Control Centre (OCC) holds the line picture and authorises degraded working methods.

questions.q: The step-by-step order of Ops-Maintenance coordination for a night work is:
options: Plan the possession → take protection/permit → hand over → do the work → certify fitness → hand back → resume service
Do the work → inform Operations Control Centre (OCC) later → resume service
questions.explain: The order matters: protection before work, certification before service.

questions.q: 'Graceful degradation' in operations means that when parts of the system fail, it should:
options: Stop everything at once, whatever has failed
Lose its functions in a planned order, keeping the safety functions working the longest
Keep running at full speed until repaired
questions.explain: A well-designed system sheds comfort and capacity first and protection last — service gets slower, but it never gets unsafe silently.

questions.q: After a degraded-mode incident is fully cleared, normal working should be restored only when:
options: Any station staff member announces it
The Operations Control Centre (OCC) confirms all systems are proved healthy and formally declares normal working
The next train driver decides on arrival
questions.explain: Return to normal is a formal step: the Operations Control Centre (OCC) restores the timetable only after every affected system is tested and certified fit.

questions.q: Scenario: A technician must check a piece of equipment inside a station equipment room during traffic hours. The work needs no track access and does not affect train running. The correct approach is to:
options: Refuse all work during traffic hours, whatever it is
Allow it under the permit-to-work system with the station's knowledge, since no possession is needed
Stop all trains while he works
Let him enter without informing anyone
questions.explain: Not every job needs a possession. Off-track work that cannot affect running is controlled by a permit and local supervision, not by stopping the service.

questions.q: Degraded-mode working raises the risk of human error mainly because:
options: Staff must do unfamiliar manual tasks under time pressure, so extra checks and supervision are needed
questions.explain: Manual working replaces automatic protection with human steps; workload and stress rise, so railways add confirmations, read-backs and supervision in degraded mode.

questions.q: Scenario: In an abnormal situation, a signalling maintainer must urgently enter the track area to repair a failed cable. Even in the emergency, he may enter only:
options: Whenever he finds a gap between trains
Under a responsible person's control, with the section protected and the Operations Control Centre (OCC) informed
By crossing from the nearest platform without telling anyone
questions.explain: Urgency never cancels protection. Emergency access is still authorised, protected and communicated — most trackside deaths happen during 'quick' unprotected entries.
